name: Baseline 1080p
blurb: Lean 1080p build that skips nothing essential. Upgrade path on the GPU.

parts.name: Ryzen 5 5500
parts.why: Cheapest current chip that never bottlenecks an entry GPU at 1080p.

alternatives.name: Core i5-14600KF
alternatives.why: Intel on the cheaper LGA1700 platform; reuses the DDR4 kit in this build.

parts.name: Radeon RX 7600
parts.why: Best cost-per-frame at 1080p high in our benchmark set.

alternatives.name: GeForce RTX 5060
alternatives.why: NVIDIA option at this tier — DLSS 4 and stronger ray tracing for about $50 more.

parts.name: B550M PRO-VDH
parts.why: Cheapest board on our QVL with a proper VRM for this CPU.

alternatives.name: PRO B760M-A DDR4
alternatives.why: Pairs with the Core i5 and keeps this build's DDR4 memory.

parts.name: 16GB DDR4-3200 CL16
parts.why: Dual-channel 16GB is the floor for modern titles; 3200 is free performance.

parts.name: P3 1TB NVMe
parts.why: Fast enough for game loads at the lowest cost per TB we track.

alternatives.name: P3 Plus 2TB NVMe
alternatives.why: Doubles capacity and adds Gen4 speed; still the cheapest per-TB drive we track.

alternatives.name: 990 PRO 4TB NVMe
alternatives.why: 4TB of DRAM-cached Gen4 — a big jump at this tier, but you never manage installs again.

parts.name: CX550 550W Bronze
parts.why: 160 W of headroom over measured peak draw.

parts.name: AIR 100 ARGB
parts.why: Mesh airflow and fans included keeps the fan budget at zero.

alternatives.name: AIR 100 ARGB White
alternatives.why: Same case, white finish and white fans, about $5 more.

name: Value 1080p+
blurb: Balanced parts, current-gen platform, room to move to 1440p later.

parts.name: Ryzen 5 7600
parts.why: AM5 entry point — socket support runs years past this build.

alternatives.name: Core Ultra 5 245K
alternatives.why: More cores for productivity; roughly level in games, needs the Intel board.

parts.name: GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 8GB
parts.why: Clears 100 FPS at 1080p ultra across our whole title set.

alternatives.name: Radeon RX 9060 XT 16GB
alternatives.why: Twice the VRAM for about $20 more; trades DLSS 4 for FSR.

parts.name: B650M Pro RS
parts.why: Wi-Fi onboard and DDR5-6000 on the QVL without paying for X670.

alternatives.name: B860 Tomahawk Wi-Fi
alternatives.why: The sensible Arrow Lake board; carries the Core Ultra 5 and keeps Wi-Fi.

parts.name: 32GB DDR5-6000 CL30
parts.why: 6000 CL30 is the Ryzen sweet spot — matched to the memory controller.

alternatives.name: 64GB DDR5-6000 CL30
alternatives.why: Two-DIMM 64GB — headroom for heavy multitasking or creative work.

parts.name: SN770 1TB NVMe
parts.why: Gen4 speeds for near-Gen3 money; DirectStorage ready.

alternatives.name: SN770 2TB NVMe
alternatives.why: Same drive, double the capacity — no speed penalty.

alternatives.name: 990 PRO 4TB NVMe
alternatives.why: Jumps to 4TB and a full-DRAM controller in one move.

parts.name: MAG A650BN 650W Gold
parts.why: 650 W covers transient GPU spikes with 40% margin.

parts.name: Pop Air mATX
parts.why: Quiet-leaning airflow case with clean cable routing.

alternatives.name: Pop Air mATX White
alternatives.why: Same chassis in white with a clear side panel.

name: Core 1440p·144
blurb: Our most-recommended configuration. GPU-forward, no bottleneck at 1440p.

parts.name: Ryzen 7 7700
parts.why: Eight cores holds 1% lows in open-world titles without pushing the budget.

alternatives.name: Core Ultra 7 265K
alternatives.why: Twenty cores for mixed work; trails the 7700 slightly in pure gaming, needs the Intel board.

parts.name: GeForce RTX 5070
parts.why: Median 112 FPS at 1440p ultra across your selected games.

alternatives.name: Radeon RX 9070
alternatives.why: Raster-comparable to the 5070 with 16GB; about $100 more, weaker ray tracing.

parts.name: B650 Tomahawk Wi-Fi
parts.why: Overbuilt VRM and 4× M.2 — the upgrade-friendly pick on AM5.

alternatives.name: B860 Tomahawk Wi-Fi
alternatives.why: Matching LGA1851 board for the Core Ultra 7; Wi-Fi 7 and 4× M.2.

parts.name: 32GB DDR5-6000 CL30
parts.why: Two DIMMs leaves both remaining slots free for a later 64GB move.

alternatives.name: 64GB DDR5-6000 CL30
alternatives.why: Skip the later upgrade and start at 64GB across two DIMMs.

parts.name: 990 EVO 2TB NVMe
parts.why: 2TB is the practical floor once three or four modern titles are installed.

alternatives.name: 990 PRO 4TB NVMe
alternatives.why: Steps up to 4TB and a full-DRAM controller for sustained write speed.

parts.name: RM750e 750W Gold
parts.why: Native 12V-2×6 connector and ATX 3.1 transient compliance.

parts.name: Lancool 216
parts.why: Best measured thermals per dB in this price class.

alternatives.name: Lancool 216 White
alternatives.why: Same airflow, white finish and white fans.

name: Performance 1440p
blurb: High-refresh 1440p with 4K headroom and a cache-heavy CPU for 1% lows.

parts.name: Ryzen 7 7800X3D
parts.why: 3D cache lifts 1% lows in sim and open-world titles more than any clock bump.

alternatives.name: Core Ultra 7 265K
alternatives.why: Intel has no 3D-cache equivalent — you trade some gaming 1% lows for more threads.

parts.name: GeForce RTX 5070 Ti
parts.why: 16GB frame buffer keeps 1440p ultra and 4K upscaled both in range.

alternatives.name: Radeon RX 9070 XT
alternatives.why: Matches the 5070 Ti in raster at lower cost; FSR instead of DLSS 4.

parts.name: TUF B650-E Wi-Fi
parts.why: PCIe 5.0 graphics slot for the next GPU generation.

alternatives.name: MPG Z890 Carbon Wi-Fi
alternatives.why: Z890 to get full memory clocks and Gen5 storage out of the Core Ultra 7.

parts.name: 32GB DDR5-6000 CL28
parts.why: CL28 kit binned for X3D chips; measurable in CPU-bound scenes.

alternatives.name: 64GB DDR5-6000 CL30
alternatives.why: 64GB for creative work alongside the game; a touch looser timings than the 32GB kit.

parts.name: 990 PRO 2TB NVMe
parts.why: Full-DRAM drive — sustained writes hold up under game installs.

alternatives.name: 990 PRO 4TB NVMe
alternatives.why: Same drive family at 4TB — one SSD for the whole library.

parts.name: RM850x 850W Gold
parts.why: 850 W and A- noise rating: quiet under sustained gaming load.

parts.name: North XL
parts.why: Premium acoustics and a front panel that does not look like a gaming rig.

alternatives.name: North XL (Chalk White)
alternatives.specs: ATX · white mesh · oak front · 413mm GPU
alternatives.why: The white-and-oak finish; same acoustics and clearance.

name: Flagship 4K
blurb: Built for 4K high-refresh with quiet thermals and full upgrade headroom.

parts.name: Ryzen 7 9800X3D
parts.why: Fastest gaming CPU we track; zero CPU bottleneck at any resolution.

alternatives.name: Core Ultra 9 285K
alternatives.why: A content-creation flagship — 24 cores, but it gives up the gaming lead to the X3D.

parts.name: GeForce RTX 5080
parts.why: Sustains 4K high-refresh with ray tracing enabled in our benchmark set.

alternatives.name: Radeon RX 9080 XT
alternatives.why: Stronger raster and 24GB for local AI work; trails the 5080 in ray tracing.

parts.name: ROG Strix X870E-E
parts.why: Full PCIe 5.0 lanes, Wi-Fi 7 and four Gen5 M.2 slots.

alternatives.name: MPG Z890 Carbon Wi-Fi
alternatives.why: The equivalent Intel flagship board for the Core Ultra 9.

parts.name: 32GB DDR5-6400 CL30
parts.why: A-die kit validated at 6400 on this board revision.

alternatives.name: 64GB DDR5-6400 CL32
alternatives.why: 64GB at 6400 for large scenes and timelines without dropping memory clock.

parts.name: T705 4TB NVMe
parts.why: Gen5 capacity drive — no install management needed.

parts.name: Vertex GX-1000 1000W
parts.why: 1000 W leaves headroom for a future 450 W-class GPU.

parts.name: Torrent Compact
parts.why: Highest airflow-per-noise measurement in our case index.

alternatives.name: Torrent Compact White
alternatives.why: Same airflow chassis in white with light-tinted glass.
